sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: L. T. Elevator is an equipment-led elevator and automated-parking expansion story, not yet a demonstrated maintenance annuity or compounder. The parent has grown materially, while acquisition timing exaggerates the consolidated headline. The decisive issue is converting earnings and orders into funded cash: FY26 group CFO was negative ₹16.99 crore, and current acquisition obligations sit on top of an unreconciled financial record. At the secondary ₹336 reference, BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS, not zero. This is a research Hold pending financial reliability, current funding and tradability evidence; no new-purchase conclusion or executable target price is supported.

sections.title: Research Header Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: The exact issuer is L. T. Elevator Limited, ISIN INE0TJ801010, BSE SME 544518, CIN L31909WB2008PLC128871. It is unrelated to Larsen & Toubro. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026; records were retrieved 21 October. The latest usable market observation is secondary 19 October ₹336 because 20 October is a scheduled holiday. Verified issued shares are 21,263,133; the implied equity value is ₹714.44 crore before unverified swap completion or warrant exercise. Entry 20 October 2026 and terminal 20 October 2031 define the five-calendar-year illustration, at a 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle. The ₹5 lakh position is hypothetical, not a suitability recommendation. Identity confidence is high; statutory revenue is medium; financial reliability, current acquired-perimeter funding and execution confidence are low. G1 is Conditional; G2/G3/G4 are Hold unresolved, not evidenced Fail.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: The 13 factors are assigned once: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 7, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P NS and L NS. BQS coverage is 80%; GQS 85%; IAS 20%. Exact Decimal weights, contributions, raw missing-factor bounds and final capped bounds are embedded below. Missing CAP/BAL prevent BQS; missing CAP prevents GQS. CASH 2 triggers the prescribed GQS cap 5, but does not turn an incomplete aggregate into 5. IAS is unavailable independently of its low coverage because the financial-reliability/funding/tradability gates are unresolved. None is ranking-eligible. Adverse findings are not multiplied into extra hidden numerical haircuts.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: FY26 consolidated revenue comprised ₹104.25 crore products and ₹7.09 crore services, a 6.37% service share. Equipment manufacture, installation and project handover dominate economics; recurring maintenance-only revenue, renewals, retained installed-base cohorts and segment margins were not disclosed sufficiently to value a proven annuity. Management describes D2C orders with 30% advance, 20–25% at production, 90% collected by dispatch and 10% at installation. Larger parking projects can have no advance, 50–60% at delivery and balances tied to installation/testing. Thus a nominally profitable order book can consume cash before certification. ParkSmart entered consolidation on 30 December 2024; Ricardo and Korean activities are not part of the March 2026 audited group and must not be retroactively inserted into that history.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text: Local installation capacity, service response, custom design and public-project qualifications offer useful but contestable advantages. The RHP reports FY25 West Bengal exposure 56.79%, down from 69.87% in FY24, and top-ten customers 27.55%; those figures do not prove a national moat. Its 800-unit elevator capacity/503-unit utilization differs from later management references to 600 existing units, requiring a definition/time bridge. Larger branded elevator suppliers and regional fabricators compete on safety, price, installation and maintenance; no peer relative-valuation premium is assumed without comparable scope. Proposed Korean patents and international deployments are management descriptions of the target, not independently demonstrated returns owned by listed shareholders. MOAT 5 reflects an established regional business with weak evidence for durable excess economics. Otis reported 2025 service sales USD 9,442 million, 65.43% of total, with 25.1% segment operating margin versus 4.8% new equipment. KONE reported 12.2% adjusted EBIT and EUR 1,761.3 million operating cash before financing/taxes, with Service its largest business. These primary peer economics explain why an equipment-led SME should not inherit an annuity premium; definitions and global geography differ. Aaron Industries provides a third, regional manufacturing comparator: FY26 revenue ₹92.005 crore included ₹68.9901 crore elevator cabins/doors/components and ₹23.0149 crore steel polishing. Operating EBITDA excluding other income was 19.22% of revenue, PAT ₹6.7974 crore and CFO after interest/taxes ₹7.6704 crore. Its component and steel mix is not equivalent to LT turnkey installation/parking, but positive cash conversion demonstrates why industry growth alone does not explain LT cash absorption. None of these three comparators justifies importing a maintenance-annuity multiple.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text: Use the statutory legal-parent series, not a splice of restated and acquired group statements. Revenue rose from ₹32.11 crore in FY21 to ₹70.74 crore in FY26, a 17.12% five-year CAGR, the framework's REV 7 band. Three-year CAGR is 26.77%; it is shown, not selected to improve the score. FY26 parent growth is 56.95%. There is no trajectory bonus. FY26 group revenue ₹111.34 crore versus statutory FY25 ₹54.72 crore reflects a full year of ParkSmart against about three months. RHP full-year FY25 pro forma ₹70.695 crore is a useful scale cross-check but rests on a different restated basis. Price/volume, acquired sourcing and intercompany eliminations prevent calling all reported growth organic. Annual absolute additions and both financial bases are retained in the historical tables.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The opportunity is to expand domestic elevators, parking and direct-to-consumer distribution while integrating overseas technology. May management reported a ₹250 crore order book excluding Ricardo, with roughly 55% elevators and 45% parking; August reported target backlog ₹65 crore and bids ₹700 crore. These are different dates/perimeters. The ₹100 crore home-elevator ARR label means annualized order bookings, not recurring contracted revenue. Neither bids nor order run-rate are added to firm orders in the model. The ₹25 crore facility and Q4 FY27 commissioning are forward commitments, not achieved productive capacity. CAP remains NS because incremental capital, acquired opening assets and attributable matured profit cannot be reconciled. The legal-parent revenue series can measure sales scale, but purchased ParkSmart supplies, subsidiary investment and unbridged goodwill/reserves prevent interpreting the same parent perimeter as a clean matured organic capital-return cohort. The 13–18% nominal cost-of-capital range is an analytical comparison range, not an estimated precise WACC. GQS is NS, with a prescribed cap 5 if missing capital evidence is later resolved without curing persistent cash weakness.

sections.title: Management Governance and Execution
sections.text: The positive evidence is a real operating history, increased manufacturing output, reported facility groundbreaking, an actual July equity issue and unmodified financial-statement/internal-control opinions. The counterevidence is not merely generic SME risk. FY25 CARO lists 20 vehicle-loan installment delays of 4–55 days, totaling ₹7.77 lakh of due-date events; that is not a claim that the amount remains overdue. FY25 and FY26 bank-return disagreements recur, with January FY26 statements not submitted. Family remuneration is ₹2.9165 crore, about 17.1% of group PAT, but approval/arm's-length disclosures and no substantiated diversion must be preserved. The CSR board report's unspent ₹8.85 lakh/transfer-pending disclosure conflicts with the note saying CSR does not apply. This is smaller than the consolidation issue and does not independently establish severe misconduct. GOV 4 and EXEC 5 distinguish material transparency weakness from an evidenced integrity failure.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: The later annual report reports FY26 group PAT ₹17.02 crore, operating EBITDA ₹26.33 crore excluding other income, and CFO negative ₹16.99 crore. Working capital absorbed ₹39.66 crore: receivables ₹23.78 crore, other current assets ₹15.63 crore and inventory ₹3.16 crore, partly offset by payables/liabilities. Cash capex ₹10.47 crore is additional investing outflow, not the explanation for weak CFO. Parent FY24–26 cumulative CFO/PAT is -1.39×. The group cash-flow statement classifies ₹37.53 crore equity proceeds in investing; a transparent illustrative reclassification is retained. The May-to-annual CFO change is ₹2.60 crore and remains unbridged. More decisively, group reserves add parent profit ₹9.5591 crore rather than group PAT ₹17.0207 crore; the ₹7.4616 crore gap almost matches goodwill's ₹7.4619 crore decline. This could understate goodwill/reserves if no valid consolidation adjustment exists; it is not asserted as fraud. RHP FY25 Annexure IX also does not reconcile its principal statements. The full main/IFC/audit-trail records were inspected; FY26 standalone CARO Annexure A is referenced but not located, so no claim of a completely clean annexure package is made.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text: The explicit model is a dated equipment/service/overseas sum-of-parts exit-earnings model linked to annual cash, working capital, capex, debt, taxes, minority claims and dilution. Domestic revenue includes Ricardo downstream sales net of manufacturer-to-retailer eliminations; Ricardo's 461,000 shares are counted once, with no fictitious cash purchase. Korean ownership is 66.445% before the specified buyback and mathematically 99.6675% after it, not an assumed 100%. Purchase/buyback cash and unknown target debt are stressed. SOTP is preferable to a mechanically precise DCF while acquisition opening capital and cash are unresolved; historical P/E, EV/EBITDA, P/B and FCF yield are only mixed-date cross-checks. Three full cases, nine growth/multiple combinations, nine funding/operating stresses and 12/15/18% hurdles are embedded. All ordinary IRRs and entry prices are null. Non-rescue paths cannot be made investable by ignoring a pre-entry floor breach. Rescue is a separate counterfactual with whole-share issuance, 3% fees and 20% discount; its returns are not available investment outcomes. The reverse solver reports no feasible funded crossing, not its search endpoint as a required growth rate.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear case is joint failure of collections, commissioning and integration rather than a simple sales slowdown. Aged receivables/unbilled projects and inventory require funding while new capacity and Korean payments consume cash; lower margins and a normalizing exit multiple then limit capital-raising ability. The model links 30 extra collection days, 3 percentage-points lower margins, 50% capex overrun, weaker INR, target debt and partial guarantee calls. Shareholders can suffer permanent dilution or loss of operating capacity even if reported PAT remains positive. Existing cash is not silently turned into debt when the algebra goes negative. Risk is High, not certain insolvency: the parent has real equipment activity and raised real cash in July. The unresolved question is whether published current resources actually cover remaining commitments under credible stress.

sections.title: Five Times and Ten Times Feasibility
sections.text: Over five calendar years, 5× and 10× shareholder wealth require approximately 38.0% and 58.5% annualized gains before taxes and execution costs. At ₹336 these imply terminal prices ₹1,680 and ₹3,360, before adjusting for future financing dilution. The embedded model computes required equity capitalization on the post-swap base and retains further dilution separately. Domestic equipment can grow, but a services share of only 6.37%, cash-consuming expansion, uncertain acquisitions and a limited demonstrated incremental-return record do not support either outcome as a base expectation. Backlog, bid pipeline or a management ARR-booking label cannot be capitalized as guaranteed multibagger revenue.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: First obtain an auditor-supported ₹7.46 crore goodwill/reserves bridge and an RHP-to-statutory FY25 reconciliation; unresolved balances keep G2 on Hold. Track bank-return differences monthly, with a target of no unexplained material variance and no missed submissions. Require subsequent-period CFO to turn positive with lower receivable/unbilled intensity rather than relying on another equity issue. Verify Q4 FY27 commissioning, final cash cost, actual utilized output and incremental contribution after working capital. Obtain current unspent July proceeds, target debt/cash, Korean closing/buyback documents and the 3,325-share residual bridge. Verify Ricardo allotment and end-customer revenue eliminations. Track service renewals and maintenance margins separately. Monitor tax/guarantee/gratuity claims and actual warrant exercise, not optional proceeds. Finally verify current BSE lot, surveillance, circuits and 20/60 session primary turnover before any implementation conclusion.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification is Hold pending evidence, equipment-led growth/acquisition special situation; compounder designation is not supported. This is neither Avoid-governance nor an evidenced funding Fail. The framework matrix cannot be applied as if NS were a low numerical score. A lower quote alone cannot cure unreliable financial bridges or unverified financing. Resolution requires auditable financial and acquisition accounts plus a conservative current funding bridge and venue-level execution evidence. Thereafter the same model can be rerun at a verified price, with genuine optional exercise money and all claims counted once. This report is research, not personal investment advice, a trade instruction or an assurance of liquidity.

sections.title: Sources Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual reports, prospectus, statutory historical statements and dated issuer transaction/operating disclosures underpin company facts. The mirrored conference transcript and holiday circular are labeled; secondary price/volume is not promoted to exchange verification. Originals were read locally but are excluded from analytical backups, which retain only safe extracts, source URLs/hashes and reproducible calculations. Reproducing these files checks arithmetic, not fresh authentication of original source publications. Forecast margins, growth, working-capital ratios, capex, FX, issue costs and target starting balances are analyst assumptions with stress tests. No acquisition closing, 100% ownership, warrant exercise, released collateral or unspent cash is invented. Open questions are explicitly attached to each gate and NS factor; ordinary returns remain null until they are resolved.

summary: L. T. Elevator is an equipment-led elevator and automated-parking expansion story, not yet a demonstrated maintenance annuity or compounder. The parent has grown materially, while acquisition timing exaggerates the consolidated headline. The decisive issue is converting earnings and orders into funded cash: FY26 group CFO was negative ₹16.99 crore, and current acquisition obligations sit on top of an unreconciled financial record. At the secondary ₹336 reference, BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS, not zero. This is a research Hold pending financial reliability, current funding and tradability evidence; no new-purchase conclusion or executable target price is supported.
